text:
Olivia: Heads up — deploy window T-30m for release/2026.41. No DB migrations. Canary plan: 10% for 10m, then 50% for 10m, then full. Rollback triggers: error-rate > 1.0% sustained over 2m OR p95 latency > 1.5s over 2m. Runbooks: /runbooks/deploy-exit-scenarios.md and /runbooks/rollback-playbook.md. Pin/unpin commands below. Reply with ack and monitoring owner.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy queued (canary id: canary-2026-41-a). CI link: https://ci.redwood.dev/changes/2026.41. Ops runbook link pinned in thread.

Priya: ack — monitoring on logs + synthetic checks. I'll watch error-rate and p95. Oncall is @Sam for this window.

Sam: acked. I'll be on-call for 30m after full rollout. Quick question — any new feature flags?

Olivia: only one: feature.alpha_rate_limiter = OFF by default. If we see rate spikes we'll enable with:
```
featurectl set alpha_rate_limiter=true --env=prod --reason="hotfix-rate-control"
```
(we'll call it out before flipping)

Evan: If we hit rollback criteria, what's the expected timeline for a backout? Are we doing full unpin or gradual ramp-down?

Olivia: primary plan is full repin to previous stable (2026.40) within 5m of confirmed breach. Steps: 1) stop new canaries, 2) pin service to 2026.40, 3) route traffic back to stable region if needed. See rollback-playbook.md.

Sam: pin/unpin commands for quick copy:
```
rctl pin service=api version=2026.41 --meta="release/2026.41"
rctl unpin service=api version=2026.40 --meta="rollback to stable"
rctl pin service=api version=2026.40 --reason="rollout-regressions"
```
Note: rctl pin is idempotent, pin takes effect cluster-wide within ~20s.

devops-bot: Canary metrics: https://metrics.redwood.dev/d/canary/canary-2026-41-a | Logs tail: https://logs.redwood.dev/q/canary-2026-41-a | Alert rules preloaded from runbook.

Priya: watching latency histograms and error spikes. Will call immediate backout if error >1% sustained or p95 breaches. I'll also snapshot current synthetic baseline: 1m avg errors 0.12% p95 380ms.

deploy-bot: canary progressed to 7% traffic after 4m, health checks passing (canary-2026-41-a -> 7%).

Evan: understood. If we need to force a backout with no response from release-manager, can SRE trigger with --force?

Olivia: emergency flow: run scripts/escape_hatch.sh in ops repo with --force; must post reason and evidence in this thread and notify @eng-oncall. We'll follow up with postmortem.

Priya: copying the emergency command in case:
```
git clone https://git.redwood.dev/ops/escape-hatch.git && cd escape-hatch && ./escape_hatch.sh --service api --target 2026.40 --reason "auto-backout-trigger" --notify
```
I'll hold the terminal.

Sam: canary finished 10m window, no breach. deploy-bot shows 10/10 health checks green. Rolling out to 50% now.

deploy-bot: rollout update: 50% -> 50% healthy. No alerts.

Olivia: nice. Keep comms here if any anomalies. If you initiate backout, post the exact rctl command + commit hash + link to runbook section used. We'll attach to the release notes.

Evan: ACK. Adding a small checklist to the runbook before next deploy: clarify post-backout verification steps and timeboxes.

Priya: noted — will add verification steps (smoke endpoints, read-only traces) in /runbooks/rollback-playbook.md and send a PR.

Sam: thanks team — will post final rollout status in #release-notes when 100% completes.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: 100% traffic (release/2026.41). Final metrics: error-rate 0.09%, p95 410ms. No rollback needed. Logs archived: https://logs.redwood.dev/archive/2026.41.

Olivia: Great ship. Closing window in 10m. If anyone wants to file follow-ups (postmortem blurb, runbook edits), please drop links here. :tada:
